annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Draw a convex lens with optical centre O and principal focus F. Place the object between F and O (at 10 cm). Draw a ray parallel to principal axis refracting through focus on the other side, and a ray passing straight through O. Extend both refracted rays backward with dashed lines to intersect on the same side as the object to show a virtual, erect, and magnified image. Include directional arrows on all rays.

teacherNote: Marked against: Writing the correct lens formula and substituting values with correct sign conventions (1); Calculating the position of the image (v = -30 cm) (1); Stating the nature of the image (virtual and erect) (1); Drawing the correct ray diagram with rays / directional arrows / and formed image (2). Remember to use the lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f rather than the mirror formula. When an object is placed inside the focal length of a convex lens, it always produces a virtual and erect image. Ensure ray diagrams clearly include directional arrows and the completed image.
